indicator_assessments.where_we_stand:
No TrendForce spot price data was included in today's news feed confirming any DDR5 16Gb MoM decline. The reference price of ~$39 for DDR5 16Gb and ~$970 for DDR5 RDIMM 32GB modules remains the operative baseline from prior TrendForce weekly prints. DDR4 spot weakness continues but is classified as EOL noise per the framework definition and does not constitute a trigger. This signal remains the single most critical unfired Tier 1 indicator in the entire framework — its absence is the primary reason the base case peak window remains 4 months out rather than imminent.

The supply backdrop is actively working against this signal firing in the near term. Today's news confirms SK Hynix is in a 'zero supply' era with margins above 70%, and Micron's HBM is sold out. The Chinese DDR5 acceleration story (CXMT/YMTC reaching 8000 MT/s speeds) is the most plausible near-term catalyst for eventual DDR5 spot softening — if Chinese makers achieve volume production of competitive DDR5 in H2 2026, spot prices could face incremental pressure from the commodity end of the market even while HBM remains tight. This bifurcation (commodity DDR5 softening while HBM stays firm) is the most likely path to this signal firing.

The monitoring cadence for this indicator is TrendForce weekly spot reports published every Friday. The trigger requires two consecutive weeks of -2%+ MoW decline in DDR5 16Gb specifically — a single week of softness is insufficient. Given the current supply tightness, the earliest plausible firing window is Q3 2026, which is consistent with the base case peak window. Any analyst or broker note citing TrendForce DDR5 spot data showing even a single week of -1%+ decline should be treated as an early warning and escalated immediately.

indicator_assessments.where_we_stand:
Today's analyst actions are uniformly and aggressively bullish — the exact opposite of the trigger condition. Nomura raised SK Hynix target to 4,000,000 KRW (implying ~120% upside from current 1,819,000 KRW) and Samsung to 590,000 KRW. Mizuho raised Micron's price target on AI tailwinds. Seeking Alpha upgraded Micron with a 'completely proven me wrong' rating upgrade. The consensus data shows 26 upward EPS revisions for SK Hynix FY+1 in the last 30 days with zero downward revisions, and 26 upward for Micron with zero downward. This is maximum euphoria in analyst sentiment.

The Nomura 'this time is different' note — explicitly arguing that Samsung and SK Hynix should be benchmarked against TSMC rather than their own historical P/E multiples — is a textbook late-cycle rationalization. Historically, the moment when the most prestigious sell-side firms publish 'new paradigm' valuation frameworks for cyclical companies is within 2–4 quarters of the fundamental peak. The TSMC comparison is particularly telling: TSMC trades at 20–25x forward earnings because it is a secular growth compounder with pricing power across all semiconductor end markets. Memory makers are commodity cyclicals with 5-year EPS standard deviations exceeding 200%. The valuation reframe is analytically unsound and historically dangerous.

The absence of this signal is itself the most important data point in today's brief. With 5/7 Tier 2 signals already fired, the two remaining unfired Tier 2 signals (t2_eps_revisions and t2_spot_contract_spread) are the last guardrails before the framework shifts to Tier 3 confirmation mode. When t2_eps_revisions fires — likely triggered by the first TrendForce contract price softness or a macro shock causing hyperscaler capex guidance cuts — it will be the single most important day in this cycle analysis. Institutional holders should have pre-defined response protocols ready for that event. The current 26-up / 0-down revision skew means the eventual reversal will be sharp and non-linear, as analysts who have been uniformly bullish will face career risk in being first to downgrade.

indicator_assessments.where_we_stand:
This indicator fired on aggregate per the framework baseline and continues to intensify today. The combination of SK Hynix's $13B new memory plant announcement, Micron's $25B capex plan, and Samsung/SK Hynix R&D spending up 68% in Q1 2026 represents a new wave of incremental capex commitment on top of already-parabolic baseline spending. The critical forward-looking question is whether hyperscalers will guide 2027 capex above 2026 levels at Q2 2026 earnings (July prints) — that would be the bull-confirm scenario that extends the peak window.

The supply-side math is becoming increasingly concerning from a cycle perspective. SK Hynix's $13B plant, if brought online on a typical 24–30 month construction timeline, would add meaningful HBM and advanced DRAM capacity in H2 2027–H1 2028 — precisely the window when the current demand wave from Rubin/Blackwell-class AI accelerators will be maturing and the next architectural generation (post-Rubin) will still be in ramp. This is the classic late-cycle capex trap: decisions made at peak demand visibility create supply that arrives at or after the demand inflection point.

The Samsung/SK Hynix R&D spending surge of 68% in Q1 2026 is a particularly important data point that is often overlooked in capex analyses. R&D spending at this level signals that both companies are racing to develop next-generation HBM architectures (HBM4, HBM4E) and advanced DRAM nodes simultaneously. This competitive intensity — both companies spending aggressively on both capex and R&D — is a hallmark of late Phase 4 behavior. Historically, the period of maximum R&D + capex spending coincides with the period of maximum supply overshoot risk, as both companies are building capacity for a technology generation that may face demand uncertainty by the time it reaches volume production. The next key monitoring event is Q2 2026 hyperscaler earnings in July, where 2027 capex guidance will be the single most important data point for updating the bull/bear probability split.

indicator_assessments.name: Supplier inventory rebuilds 2-3 → 4-5 weeks
indicator_assessments.description: Memory makers' inventory weeks rising from record lows.
indicator_assessments.what_to_look_for: SK Hynix or Micron inventory weeks crossing 4 in TrendForce monthly print or earnings disclosure. Currently 2-3 weeks.
indicator_assessments.where_we_stand:
Supplier inventory remains at record lows of 2-3 weeks per prior TrendForce data. Today's 'zero supply' language from SK Hynix is the strongest possible confirmation that inventory weeks have not increased — in fact, the framing suggests inventory may be at or below the low end of the 2-3 week range. The Samsung 45,000–50,000 worker strike threat (5 days away per Tech Times) is a new wildcard: if the strike materializes and disrupts production, it could paradoxically keep supplier inventory even lower for longer, extending the tight supply narrative.

The path to this indicator firing runs through one of three scenarios: (1) a demand shock that causes buyers to reduce orders faster than suppliers can cut production, causing inventory to build involuntarily; (2) a deliberate supplier decision to build strategic inventory ahead of a technology transition (e.g., HBM3E to HBM4 transition creating temporary HBM3E overstock); or (3) a supply ramp outpacing demand absorption in commodity DDR5, which is the most plausible near-term path given Chinese DDR5 acceleration. None of these scenarios are visible in today's data.

The Samsung strike threat deserves specific attention as a potential supply-side shock. A 45,000–50,000 worker walkout at Samsung's memory chip plants would be the largest labor action in Korean semiconductor history. If it materializes, the immediate effect would be production disruption at Samsung's DRAM and NAND fabs, which could tighten supply further in the near term. However, the medium-term effect could be more complex: if Samsung is forced to offer significant wage concessions, it would increase the company's cost structure at a time when it is already losing HBM market share to SK Hynix. This could accelerate Samsung's competitive disadvantage and potentially lead to capacity rationalization decisions that would eventually show up as inventory normalization. Monitor the strike situation closely over the next 5 days.

If memory pure-plays continue to underperform SOX by a cumulative >10% over the 5-day window ending approximately May 22, 2026, the signal will be fully confirmed. The prior March 2026 firing was reversed by the May rally — the question is whether this re-firing represents the beginning of sustained underperformance or another temporary flush that will be reversed by the next positive catalyst.

The structural context for this signal is important. The 1-month and 3-month performance data shows extraordinary outperformance by memory names: SK Hynix +64.91% in 1 month, +105.45% in 3 months; Micron +58.49% in 1 month, +76.11% in 3 months; Samsung +30.99% in 1 month, +62.90% in 3 months. When stocks that have doubled or tripled in 3 months begin to underperform their sector index, it is often the first visible sign that the marginal buyer has been exhausted. The combination of extreme recent outperformance and the re-firing of the relative strength signal is a meaningful warning. However, the signal requires 5-day confirmation before being classified as fully fired — a single-session flush driven by macro factors (e.g., tariff news, Fed commentary) can reverse quickly.
